Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:10:1.hebrew: בגדיש דעלמא - אמאי משלם חררה? הא שן הוא, ובעינן שדה אחר דניזק, וליכא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:10:1.english: On a stack [of grain] belonging to someone else - Why does he pay [for] the cake? Surely it is [damage of] Tooth, and we require "the field of another" — [that] of the injured party — and [that] is not [the case here].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:11:1.english: You may resolve - For since he pays [for] the cake.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:11:2.english: That the mouth of his cow - of the damager, which eats in the courtyard of the injured party.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:1:1.hebrew: בנזקי ממונו - דכתיב כי תצא אש, דמשמע מעצמה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:1:1.english: With damage caused by his property - For it is written, "If fire breaks out," which implies [that it broke out] on its own.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:1:2.english: With damage [caused by] his body - For [the verse] calls him "the one who kindled [the fire]."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:2:1.hebrew: היכי משכחת לה - אילו אדם זורק חץ והזיק בטמון, לא מיחייב בנזק? הא קיימא לן בהאי פירקין (דף כו:): "פצע תחת פצע" — לחייב את השוגג כמזיד, ואונס כרצון. לישנא אחרינא: האי חץ, לעולם בטמון הוא נכנס ומזיק. ולא שמעתי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:2:1.english: How can you find it - If a person shoots an arrow and it damages [something] concealed, is he not liable for the damage? Why, we hold in this chapter (26b): "Wound for wound" — to render liable one who acts unintentionally just as one who acts intentionally, and [one who acts under] duress just as [one who acts] willingly. Another version: This arrow always enters into a concealed [place] and damages. But I have not heard [this].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:3:1.english: And it was satisfactory for him - And he answers it thus:

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:3:2.english: And a fence collapsed - Of the courtyard.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:3:3.hebrew: שלא מחמת דליקה - דאי מחמת דליקה, חציו הם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:3:3.english: Not due to the fire - For if [it fell] due to the fire, [the flames] are his arrows.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:3:4.hebrew: דכלו לו חציו - שבשעה שהדליק האש, דהיינו זריקת חץ, לא היה ראוי להזיק בחצר אחרת:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:3:4.english: For his arrows were depleted - For at the time that he lit the fire, which is the shooting of the arrow, it was not capable of causing damage in another courtyard.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:5:1.hebrew: אית ליה נמי משום ממונו - והיכא דליכא לחיוביה משום חציו ואיכא לחיוביה משום ממונו, מחייבינן ליה. הלכך, לענין גלוי, אע"ג דכלו לו חציו, חייב משום ממונו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:5:1.english: He also holds [that liability is] due to his property - And where it is not possible to obligate him due to his arrows, and it is possible to obligate him due to his property, we obligate him. Therefore, with respect to exposed [items], even though his arrows have been spent, he is liable due to his property.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:5:2.hebrew: וכגון שהיה לו לגודרה - בטרם תעבור הדליקה שם, היה לו שהות ויכול לגודרה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:5:2.english: And for example, where he had [the ability] to fence it in - Before the fire passed there, he had time and was able to fence it in.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:5:3.hebrew: ולא גדרה - דאע"ג דליכא לחיוביה אהבער ראשון, מתחייב על שם סופו, שלא שימר גחלתו לגדור בפניה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:5:3.english: But he did not fence it in - For even though he cannot be held liable for the initial kindling, he becomes liable on account of its aftermath, for he did not guard his coal [by] fencing before it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:5:4.english: It is his ox and he did not strike [it] in its face - This is like one who brings his ox into a pen and did not lock [the door] before it, and it went out and caused damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:6:1.hebrew: וכי מאחר דמאן דאית ליה משום חציו אית ליה נמי משום ממונו מאי בינייהו - היכא דגחלת שלו היתה, מאי איכא בין ר' יוחנן דמחייב ליה משום תרתי לר"ל דלא מחייב ליה אלא משום חדא? דהא על כרחך היכא דגחלת שלו נמי פליגי, דהא אמרן לעיל לרבי יוחנן אשו משום חציו, אלמא באשו נמי פליגי היכא דגחלת שלו. בשלמא עד השתא, דשמעינן משום חציו דוקא ולאו משום ממונו — וכדאמרת "ממון אית ביה מששא, הא לית ביה מששא" — איכא בינייהו היכא דאיתיה ממונו וליתיה חציו, כי הך דנפלה גדר, דכלו לו חציו, דלמ"ד משום חציו דוקא פטור; אבל השתא דלתרוייהו חייב, מאי בינייהו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:6:1.english: And since the one who holds [that liability for fire is] due to his arrows also holds [that it is] due to his property, what is [the difference] between them - Where the coal was his, what is [the difference] between Rabbi Yochanan, who holds him liable on two [grounds], and Reish Lakish, who holds him liable on only one? For perforce, they also disagree where the coal was his, since we stated above that according to Rabbi Yochanan, "his fire is due to his arrows" — thus [it is evident that] they also disagree regarding "his fire" where the coal is his. Granted, until now, when we understood [Rabbi Yochanan's view to be] specifically due to his arrows and not due to his property — as you said, "property has substance, whereas this [fire] has no substance" — the difference between them was where his property is present and his arrows are not, such as that case where a fence fell, where his arrows have ceased, for according to the one who says [liability is] specifically due to his arrows, he is exempt. But now that according to both of them he is liable, what is [the difference] between them?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:7:1.hebrew: לחייבו בד' דברים - למ"ד משום חציו נמי מחייבינן ליה: אם שרף אשו יד אדם, חייב בארבעה דברים — נזק, וצער, ריפוי, ושבת — אבל בבושת לא, דאמרינן בשילהי פירקין: "אינו חייב על הבושת עד שיהא מתכוין". אבל ד' דברים חייב, דפשיעה היא, דהוה ליה לאסוקי אדעתיה שהרוח מוליכתה, וכדאמרינן בשילהי פירקין: "נפל מן הגג ברוח מצויה, חייב בד' דברים ופטור על הבושת". למ"ד משום ממונו — פטור. והוא הדין נמי דאיכא בינייהו כל הני דלעיל, כלב וגמל: דלמ"ד משום חציו חייב, דהא ממונו אע"ג דלאו חציו וחציו אע"ג דלאו ממונו אית ליה; ולמאן דלית ליה חציו פטור, אא"כ מסכסכת, כדאוקימנא לעיל. והאי דנקט ד' דברים, משום דאפילו היכא דהגחלת שלו, משמע לו דיש חילוק בדבריהם, ועוד דמילתא דשכיח היא. מפי המורה שמעתי, אבל לשון ראשון נראה לי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:7:1.english: To hold him liable for four things - According to the one who says [fire is] due to "his arrows," we also hold him liable [for them]: if his fire burned a person's hand, he is liable for four things — damage, pain, medical expenses, and loss of livelihood — but not for humiliation, as we say at the end of our chapter: "He is not liable for humiliation unless he intends [to inflict it]." However, [for the other] four things he is liable, because it is negligence, as he should have considered that the wind carries it, and as we say at the end of our chapter: "[If] he fell from the roof in a common wind, he is liable for four things and exempt for humiliation." According to the one who says [fire is] due to "his property," he is exempt [from them]. And the same applies as well that all those [cases mentioned] above — [the] dog and [the] camel — are [practical differences] between them: for according to the one who says [it is] due to "his arrows," he is liable, since he holds [liability for] "his property" even though it is not "his arrows," and [for] "his arrows" even though it is not "his property"; whereas according to the one who does not hold [the principle of] "his arrows," he is exempt unless it spreads [the fire], as we established above. And the reason [the Gemara] stated "four things" is because even where the coal is his, it seemed to him that there is a distinction in their words [in this case], and furthermore, because it is a common occurrence. I heard [this explanation] from the mouth of the teacher, but the first explanation seems [correct] to me.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:8:1.hebrew: מאן חייב בעל הכלב - אמתניתין מהדר, דקתני על הגדיש משלם חצי נזק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:8:1.english: Who is liable? The owner of the dog - [The Gemara] is referring back to the Mishnah, which teaches: "For the stack of grain he pays half-damages."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:8:2.hebrew: ה"ג וליחייב נמי בעל הגחלת - דהא בין מר ובין מר משום ממונו אית להו. הלכך, לר' יוחנן, דאמר לעיל על הגדיש משלם חצי נזק דצרורות הן, לשלם בעל הגחלת חצי האחר, דהא ממונו הוא; וריש לקיש, דאמר על הגדיש כולו הוי פטור, לשלם בעל הגחלת כוליה. וקס"ד דגחלת דחד, וחררה וגדיש דחד:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:8:2.english: Thus we read [the text]: And let the owner of the coal also be liable - For both this [master] and that [master] hold [that fire is] due to his property. Therefore, according to Rabbi Yochanan, who said above [that] for the stack he pays half-damages because it is [a case of] pebbles, let the owner of the coal pay the other half, since it is his property; and [according to] Reish Lakish, who said [that] for the entire stack he is exempt, let the owner of the coal pay all of it. And [the Gemara] initially assumed that the coal belonged to one [person], and the cake and the stack belonged to another [person].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:8:3.hebrew: בששימר גחלתו - שנעל דלתות ביתו יפה, ואונס הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:8:3.english: Where he safeguarded his coal - For he locked the doors of his house well, and it is [a case of] unavoidable accident.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:9:1.hebrew: זאת אומרת - מדחייב לבעל כלב אחררה נזק שלם, אלמא לאו שינוי הוא זה שחתר את הדלת:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:9:1.english: That is to say - Since [it] obligates the owner of the dog [to pay] full damages for the cake, evidently it is not an unusual act that it burrowed [under] the door.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23a:9:2.english: That ordinary doors are [prone to being] burrowed under by a dog - And do not say [that] it is unusual and [therefore] he pays half-damages.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23a:11:1.hebrew: תפשוט דפי פרה כחצר הניזק דמי - תימה, דאמאי לא פשיט משאר בבי דמתני' דתנן: "השן מועדת לאכול הראוי לה", ומההיא ד"אכלה מצידי הרחבה ומתוך החנות"? ועוד, אותם שהיו מדקדקין "משיסה בו את הכלב", למה לא הביאו מתניתין "כלב שנטל חררה" דדייק מינה השתא? ועוד, מאי קאמר "מאי בעי ריפתך בפומא דכלבאי", כיון שהכלב לקחה? ונראה לר"י, דמכל הנהו דמתניתין לא מצי למפשט, ולא מההיא ד"נטל חררה", משום דס"ד דאם לקחה הבהמה פירות בחצר הניזק ואכלה ברשות הרבים [או בחצר המזיק] — חייב, דמחייבינן בלקיחה לחודא; וכן הסברא נוטה, דכיון דפשע בלקיחה, מה לנו באכילה? והא דממעטינן מ"שדה אחר" רשות הרבים, היינו לקיחה. וקמבעיא ליה כגון אם הושיט פירות בפי פרה חש"ו ועכו"ם דלאו בני תשלומין נינהו, וכגון שהבהמה לא היתה יכולה ליקח אם לא שהושיט לה: ואי כחצר הניזק דמי — חייב בעל הפרה, ואי כחצר המזיק דמי — פטור, כיון שנתנו אחר לתוך פיה. והא דקאמר "תפשוט", לאו ממתני', אלא מסוגיא דשמעתין, דאוקמה "אכלה בגדיש דבעל החררה" — שמע מינה דבעו לקיחה ואכילה בחצר [הניזק], אף על פי שאין טעם בדבר זה, מה צורך באכילה, אלא דגזירת הכתוב הוא. ותפשוט כשנתן אחר לתוך פיה דחייב, דכחצר הניזק דמיא; דאי כחצר המזיק דמיא, ומצי אמר ליה "מאי בעי ריפתך בפומא דחיותאי", ה"נ מצי א"ל "מאי בעי ריפתך בפומא דכלבאי". וזה הלשון לאו דוקא, דהכא לא שייך לשון זה שהכלב לקח מעצמו, אלא כלומר: כיון דגזירת הכתוב דבעי' אכילה בחצר הניזק, ואי פי פרה כחצר המזיק, אפילו כי אכלה בגדיש דבעל החררה הוי אכילה בחצר המזיק; ואגב דשייך לשון זה בנתן אחר לתוך פיה, נקט ליה. ומייתי "משיסה בו את הכלב", דשסוי מיקרי אפילו הכניס יד חבירו בפי הכלב או הנחש, והשיך היינו דתחב ודחק שיני הכלב ונחש בבשר חבירו — וא"כ אמאי חייב בעל הכלב? והלא ידו בחצר המזיק הוא, ולימא ליה "מאי בעי ידך בפומא דכלבאי"? והא דקאמר "שן דחייב רחמנא היכי משכחת לה", אף על גב דמשכחת לה שפיר כגון שהלקיחה היתה בחצר הניזק, אלא משום דפשטיה דקרא משמע שהביעור היתה בחצר הניזק, קבעי היכי משכחת לה. ובריש מסכת שבת (דף ג:) איכא נמי "תפשוט" מסוגיא דשמעתין, דקאמר "תפשוט מדבעי רב ביבי בר אביי":
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23a:11:1.english: Resolve [from here] that the mouth of a cow is like the courtyard of the injured party - It is astonishing: why did [the Gemara] not resolve [this dilemma] from the other clauses of the Mishnah, where we learned: "The tooth is forewarned to eat what is fit for it," and from that [clause]: "[If] it ate from the sides of the plaza or from inside the shop"? And furthermore, those who were trying to deduce [the answer] from "[If] he incited the dog against him" — why did they not cite our Mishnah, "A dog that took a cake [baked on coals]," from which [the Gemara] infers [this] now? And furthermore, what does [the Gemara] mean by saying, "What is your bread doing in my dog's mouth?" given that the dog took it [on its own]? And it appears to R' Yitzchak that from all those [cases] in the Mishnah one cannot resolve [it], nor from that [case] of "[a dog that] took a cake," because one might have thought that if the animal took produce in the courtyard of the injured party and ate [it] in the public domain [or in the courtyard of the damager], [the owner] is liable, for we hold [him] liable based on the taking alone; and logic also inclines toward this, for since [the animal] acted negligently in taking [it], what does the eating matter to us? And that which we exclude the public domain from [the verse] "another's field" [refers to] the taking. Rather, [the Gemara's] dilemma is in a case such as where a deaf-mute, an imbecile, a minor, or an idolater — who are not subject to paying compensation — extended produce into the mouth of a cow, and where the animal would not have been able to take [it] had [that person] not extended [it] to it: if [the cow's mouth] is like the courtyard of the injured party, the owner of the cow is liable; and if it is like the courtyard of the damager, he is exempt, since another person placed it inside its mouth. And when [the Gemara] says "Resolve [it]," [it is] not from the Mishnah [itself], but rather from the reasoning of our sugya, which established [the Mishnah's case as where] "it ate [it] on a stack of grain belonging to the owner of the cake" — deduce from this that we require both taking and eating in the courtyard [of the injured party], even though there is no logical reason for this matter — why is there a need for eating [there]? — rather, it is a Scriptural decree. And [therefore] resolve [that] when another person placed [produce] into its mouth, [the owner] is liable, because [the mouth] is like the courtyard of the injured party; for if it were like the courtyard of the damager, and he could say to him, "What is your bread doing in my animal's mouth?" here too [in the Mishnah's case] he could say to him, "What is your bread doing in my dog's mouth?" And this phrasing is not exact, for here [in the case of the dog] this phrasing does not apply, since the dog took [the cake] on its own; rather, it means to say: since it is a Scriptural decree that we require eating in the courtyard of the injured party, if the mouth of a cow were like the courtyard of the damager, even when [the dog] ate it on the stack of the owner of the cake, it would be [considered] eating in the courtyard of the damager; and because this phrasing is applicable to [the case where] another person placed [produce] into its mouth, [the Gemara] used it. And [that is why] it brings [a proof] from "[If] he incited the dog against him," for "inciting" is called [so] even when he inserted his fellow's hand into the mouth of the dog or the snake, and "causing to bite" means that he thrust and pressed the teeth of the dog or snake into his fellow's flesh — and if so, why is the owner of the dog liable? Is his hand not in the courtyard of the damager, so let him say to him, "What is your hand doing in my dog's mouth?" And as for what [the Gemara] says, "In what scenario can you find [liability for] Tooth that the Merciful One obligated?" — even though you could readily find it [in a case] such as where the taking was in the courtyard of the injured party, nevertheless, because the plain meaning of the verse implies that the consuming was in the courtyard of the injured party, it asks, "In what scenario can you find it?" And at the beginning of tractate Shabbat (3b) there is also [an instance of] "resolve [it]" [derived] from the reasoning of the sugya itself, where it says, "Resolve [it] from that which Rav Bivi bar Abaye inquired."

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23a:2:1.hebrew: טמון באש דפטר רחמנא היכי משכחת לה - פי': בשלמא למ״ד אשו משום ממונו, אין תימה דפטור טמון, ואע״ג דבכל נזקי ממונו, כמו קרן, שן ורגל, חייב טמון — שבממון מצינו חילוקים בקרן, שן ורגל להלכותיהן. אבל באדם המזיק לא חלק הכתוב, דכתיב "פצע תחת פצע", ודרשינן בסוף פירקין (בבא קמא דף כו:) לחייב על השוגג כמזיד ואונס כרצון; לפיכך אין סברא לדרוש אשו משום חציו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23a:2:1.english: "How can you find [a case where] the Merciful One exempted concealed [items] in a fire?" - Explanation: Granted, according to the one who says [that liability for] one's fire is due to [its being] his property, it is not surprising that [one is] exempt [for] concealed [items], even though in all [other] damages of his property, such as Horn, Tooth, and Foot, he is liable [for] concealed [items] — because regarding property, we find distinctions in Horn, Tooth, and Foot with respect to their laws. However, regarding a person who causes damage, Scripture did not make distinctions, as it is written, "wound for wound," and we expound at the end of our chapter (Bava Kamma 26b) to hold [him] liable for unintentional [damage] as [for] intentional, and [damage by] unavoidable accident as [that done] willfully; therefore, it is not reasonable to expound [that liability for] his fire is due to [its similarity to] his arrows.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23a:6:1.hebrew: מאי בינייהו - הוה מצי למימר: איכא בינייהו כל הני דלעיל: כלב שנטל חררה ואנחי אנוחי בגדיש, דלרבי יוחנן משלם על שאר הגדיש חצי נזק, ולר"ל על שאר הגדיש פטור; ולרבי יוחנן אפילו לא הצית בגופו של עבד, קם ליה בדרבה מיניה; וטמון, היכא שלא כלו חציו, חייב לרבי יוחנן:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23a:6:1.english: What is [the difference] between them - [The Gemara] could have said: There is [a difference] between them [in] all those [cases mentioned] above: a dog that took a coal-cake and placed it upon a stack of grain, where according to Rabbi Yochanan he pays half-damages for the rest of the stack, whereas according to Reish Lakish he is exempt for the rest of the stack; and according to Rabbi Yochanan, even if he did not set fire [directly] to the body of a slave, he is subject to the greater [penalty] [and is exempt from payment]; and [regarding] concealed [property], where his arrows have not yet been spent, he is liable according to Rabbi Yochanan.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23a:8:1.hebrew: וליחייב בעל הגחלת - פירוש: גם בעל הגחלת, ולא שיפטר בעל הכלב לגמרי, כדפ"ל (דף כב. ד"ה ואי) גבי חנוני אמאי חייב. ועוד, אי בשלא שמר גחלתו ומפטר בעל הכלב, אמאי קאמר (לעיל בבא קמא יט:) מתני' באדייה אדויי ודרב הונא בעלמא איתמר? לימא דרב הונא קאי אמתני': "קשרו אדם — חייב הקושר נ"ש", ובעל התרנגול פטור, כמו הכא דפטור בעל הכלב! אלא ודאי בשלא שימר גחלתו חייב נמי בעל הכלב, ולכך לא מיתוקמא דרב הונא אמתני', ד"קשרו אדם חייב" משמע דחייב הכל הקושר, ובעל התרנגול יש לו להתחייב כמו כן:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23a:8:1.english: And let the owner of the coal be liable - Explanation: [this means] the owner of the coal as well, and not that the owner of the dog would be completely exempt, as I explained above (22a, s.v. Ve'i) regarding why the storekeeper is liable. Furthermore, if [it were the case that] when he did not guard his coal, the owner of the dog is exempt, why did [the Gemara] say (above, Bava Kamma 19b) that our Mishnah [deals with a case where the rooster] threw [the vessel] and that Rav Huna's [statement] was stated independently? Let us say [instead] that Rav Huna's [statement] refers to our Mishnah: "[if] a person tied it, the one who tied it is liable for full damages," and the owner of the rooster is exempt — just as here, where the owner of the dog [would be] exempt! Rather, certainly when he did not guard his coal, the owner of the dog is also liable; and therefore Rav Huna's [statement] cannot be established as referring to our Mishnah, for "[if] a person tied it, he is liable" implies that the one who tied it is liable for everything, whereas [in our Mishnah] the owner of the rooster ought to be liable as well.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23a:8:2.hebrew: ולחייב בעל הגחלת - האי לישנא לאו דוקא, דהא מיתוקמא דאכלה בגדיש דבעל החררה, אלא כלומר שיפטר בעל הכלב מחלקו של בעל הגחלת, ולא ישלם כי אם הרביע. וא"ת: ואמאי לא פריך "וליפטר בעל הכלב מן החררה"? ונראה מכאן לדקדק דיותר יש לאדם ליזהר עצמו שלא יזיק אחרים משלא יוזק, שמחויב לשמור גחלתו מן הכלב אע"פ שאין לו רשות ליכנס לביתו, כדי שלא יזיק אחרים, ואפשר לשמור עצמו כדי שלא יכנוס כלב כדי ליטול חררתו. וכן משמע בהמניח (לקמן בבא קמא דף לא.) בשמעתין דקדרין, דפריך: אי נתקל פושע, שני נמי ליחייב! אלמא חשיב שני פושע לחייבו בנזק שלישי, ואינו פושע לענין שיפטר ראשון בנזקיו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23a:8:2.english: But let the owner of the coal be liable - This wording is imprecise, since [the case] is established as one where [the dog] ate [the cake] on the grain stack of the owner of the cake; rather, [the Gemara] means to say that the owner of the dog should be exempt from the share of the owner of the coal, and should pay only a quarter. And if you ask: Why does [the Gemara] not challenge, "And let the owner of the dog be exempt from [paying for] the cake"? It appears from here that we can infer that a person must be more careful not to damage others than not to be damaged himself — for he is obligated to guard his coal from the dog even though [the dog] has no permission to enter his house, so that he will not damage others, [whereas] it is possible to guard oneself so that a dog does not enter to take one's cake. And so it is implied in [the chapter] HaManiach (below, Bava Kamma 31a) in our discussion of the potters, where [the Gemara] challenges: "If one who stumbles is negligent, the second one should also be liable!" Thus, the second one is considered negligent so as to obligate him for the damage of the third one, yet he is not [considered] negligent such that the first one should be exempt from [paying for] his damages.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23a:8:3.hebrew: בששימר גחלתו - וא"ת: ומה שמירה היא זו, כיון שיכול הכלב ליכנס שם בחתירה, דסתם דלתות חתורות הן אצל הכלב? וי"ל: כיון דנטר כדנטרי אינשי, לא אטרחוהו רבנן טפי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23a:8:3.english: Where he safeguarded his coal - And if you ask: What [kind of] safeguarding is this, since the dog can enter there by digging under, as ordinary doors are dug under by a dog? And one can answer: Since he guarded [it] as people guard, the Rabbis did not trouble him further.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23a:9:1.hebrew: בשחתר - ואם תאמר: ולישני כגון דנפלה גודא בליליא, וידע בעל הכלב ובעל הגחלת לא ידע? ויש לומר, דאין זה רגילות דבעל הכלב ידע ובעל הגחלת לא ידע; ולקמן גבי עיזי דבשדות, רגילות הוא לפעמים:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23a:9:1.english: Where [the dog] burrowed - And if you ask: Let [the Gemara] answer [that the case is] where a wall fell down at night, and the owner of the dog knew [about it], whereas the owner of the coal did not know? And one can say that it is not usual for the owner of the dog to know while the owner of the coal does not know; whereas later, regarding goats in the fields, it is sometimes usual.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23a:9:2.hebrew: סתם דלתות חתורות הן - תימה, דלמא משום דהוי תחילתו בפשיעה וסופו באונס, תחילתו בפשיעה משום פתיחה? ויש לומר דא"כ לא מיחייב בחתירה כ"א רביע, כי היכי דהוה מתחייב בפתיחה, שהיה בעל הגחלת מתחייב מחצה. אבל אין לתרץ דלא אמרינן תחלתו בפשיעה בבתים פתוחים וסופו באונס בנעולים, כיון דגבי נעולים לא הוי שום פשיעה, כדאמרינן בהפרה (לקמן בבא קמא דף נב:) דלא אמרינן מגו דהוי פושע לענין חרש הוי פושע לענין פקח כו', ומגו דהוי פושע לענין גמלים הוי פושע לענין שוורים — דלא דמי; דהתם ודאי לא אמרינן מגו, משום דלגבי פקח או לגבי שוורים הניזקין לא פשעי כלל, אבל הכא פושע הוא בכלב זה לענין זה הגדיש להיות ניזוק בגחלתו בפשיעה היכא שלא שמר גחלתו, לכך יש להתחייב אפילו נזוקין באונס למאן דמחייב תחילתו בפשיעה וסופו באונס:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23a:9:2.english: Ordinary doors are [deemed vulnerable to being] burrowed [under] - [This is] astonishing! Perhaps [it is] because [the case] is one where its beginning was through negligence and its end was through unavoidable accident — its beginning through negligence because of opening [the door]? And one can say that if so, he would only be liable for burrowing for a quarter [of the damage], just as he would have been liable in [a case of] opening [the door], where the owner of the coal would be liable for half. However, one cannot answer that we do not say "its beginning was through negligence" with open houses and "its end was through unavoidable accident" with locked ones, since with locked ones there is no negligence at all — as we say in [the chapter] HaParah (later, Bava Kamma 52b), that we do not say "since he was negligent with respect to a deaf-mute, he is [considered] negligent with respect to a person of sound senses, etc.," and "since he was negligent with respect to camels, he is [considered] negligent with respect to oxen" — for [the cases] are not comparable: there, we certainly do not say migo ("since..."), because with respect to a person of sound senses or with respect to the oxen that were damaged, they were not negligent at all; whereas here, he is negligent with this dog with respect to this stack of grain, [causing it] to be damaged by his coal through negligence when he did not guard his coal — therefore, he should be liable even when [the stack] is damaged through an unavoidable accident, according to the one who holds [a person] liable when its beginning was through negligence and its end was through unavoidable accident.
